name: Fixed-effect model (data-generating equation)
variables: Y_i = observed effect in study i; theta = common true effect; eps_i = sampling error of study i
notes: Model statement; implemented as model='fixed'. Book's illustration: theta = 0.60 with eps = -0.20, +0.10, -0.10 gives Y = 0.40, 0.70, 0.50.

name: Fixed-effect inverse-variance weight
variables: W_i = weight of study i; V_Yi = within-study variance of study i

name: Fixed-effect weighted mean (summary effect)
variables: M = fixed-effect summary; W_i = 1/V_Yi; Y_i = observed effect; k = number of studies
notes: Engine: model='fixed'.

name: Variance of the fixed-effect summary
variables: V_M = variance of M; W_i = fixed-effect weights

name: Standard error of the fixed-effect summary
variables: SE_M = standard error of M; V_M = variance of M
notes: Ch13 example: SE_M = 0.064.

name: 95% confidence limits of the fixed-effect summary
variables: LL_M, UL_M = lower and upper 95% limits; M = summary; SE_M = its standard error; 1.96 = standard normal 97.5th percentile
notes: Wald/z interval; engine needs ci_method='z' (default for model='fixed').

name: Z test of the fixed-effect summary
variables: Z = test statistic for H0: theta = 0; M = summary; SE_M = its standard error
notes: Tests the null that the common effect is zero in every study (log scale for ratio measures).

name: One-tailed p-value (fixed effect)
variables: Phi = standard normal cumulative distribution function; use '+' if the effect is in the expected direction and '-' otherwise
notes: Excel: =NORMSDIST(Z). Engine: 1 - Phi(x) is distributions.norm_sf(x), so p = norm_sf(|Z|) when the effect is in the expected direction and norm_sf(-|Z|) otherwise.

name: Two-tailed p-value (fixed effect)
variables: Phi = standard normal CDF; Z = M/SE_M
notes: Excel: =NORMSDIST(Z).

name: Random-effects model (data-generating equation)
variables: Y_i = observed effect; mu = grand mean of the true effects; zeta_i = theta_i - mu, deviation of study i's true effect from mu (variance tau^2); eps_i = Y_i - theta_i, sampling error (variance V_Yi)
notes: True effects usually assumed normally distributed (p. 70).

name: DerSimonian-Laird (method of moments) estimate of tau^2
variables: T^2 = estimate of the between-studies variance tau^2; Q = eq. 12.3; df = k - 1; C = eq. 12.5
notes: Sample omits the truncation rule; full book (Ch16, p. 114, NOT IN SAMPLE) and the engine set T^2 = 0 when Q < df. [note: Cochrane Handbook v6 prefers REML/Paule-Mandel (engine: models.tau2_reml, models.tau2_pm).] Ch13 example recomputed: T^2 = 0.0373.

name: Cochran's Q (computational form)
variables: Q = weighted sum of squares about the fixed-effect mean; W_i = 1/V_Yi (fixed-effect weights); Y_i = observed effects
notes: Algebraically equal to sum W_i (Y_i - M)^2, which is what the engine computes (less round-off error). Ch13 example recomputed: Q = 12.0033.

name: Degrees of freedom for Q
variables: df = degrees of freedom; k = number of studies

name: Scaling constant C for the DL estimator
variables: C = scaling factor; W_i = fixed-effect weights 1/V_Yi
notes: Returned as key 'C' by models.heterogeneity; also computed inside models.tau2_dl. Ch13 example recomputed: C = 187.698.

name: Random-effects total variance and weight
variables: V*_Yi = total variance of study i under random effects; V_Yi = within-study variance; T^2 = between-studies variance estimate; W*_i = random-effects weight
notes: Asterisk marks random-effects quantities.

name: Random-effects weighted mean (summary effect)
variables: M* = random-effects summary (estimate of mu); W*_i = random-effects weights
notes: Engine: model='random', tau2_method='DL' to match the book. [note: DL is used only to reproduce the book; Cochrane Handbook v6 prefers REML or Paule-Mandel (engine default REML).]

name: Variance of the random-effects summary
variables: V_M* = variance of M*; W*_i = random-effects weights

name: Standard error of the random-effects summary
variables: SE_M* = standard error of M*
notes: Ch13 example: 0.105. Engine attribute se_wald holds this Wald SE; se equals it only with ci_method='z' or 't'.

name: 95% confidence limits of the random-effects summary
variables: LL_M*, UL_M* = 95% limits; M* = summary; SE_M* = its standard error
notes: Wald/z interval as in the book; the engine defaults to HKSJ for random effects, so pass ci_method='z' to reproduce. [note: current guidance often prefers HKSJ/t-based intervals.]

name: Z test of the random-effects summary
variables: Z* = test statistic for H0: mu = 0 (mean of true effects is zero)
notes: Different null from the fixed-effect test (p. 83).

name: One-tailed p-value (random effects)
variables: Phi = standard normal CDF; '+' if the effect is in the expected direction, '-' otherwise
notes: Excel: =NORMSDIST(Z*). Engine: 1 - Phi(x) is distributions.norm_sf(x), so p = norm_sf(|Z*|) when the effect is in the expected direction and norm_sf(-|Z*|) otherwise.

name: Two-tailed p-value (random effects)
variables: Phi = standard normal CDF; Z* = M*/SE_M*

name: Relative weight (percent) of a study
expression: RW_i = 100 * W_i / sum_{j=1..k}(W_j)   (use W*_i under random effects)
variables: RW_i = relative weight of study i in %; W_i = fixed-effect or random-effects weight
notes: Not printed as an equation; implied by the 'Relative Weight' columns, which total 100%. Engine attribute weights_pct. Ch13 example FE 12/13/8/39/10/18%, RE 16/16/13/23/14/18%.

name: Variance of a single-group mean (one-sample design)
variables: V_Yi = within-study variance of the mean; sigma = SD of participants' scores; n = sample size of the study
notes: Engine has no single-mean measure; such data can be pooled via the generic (GEN) yi/vi input.

name: Fixed-effect weight and summary SE for k equal one-group studies
expression: W_i = 1/(sigma^2/n) = n/sigma^2 ; V_M = 1/(k*n/sigma^2) = sigma^2/(k*n) ; SE_M = sqrt(sigma^2/(k*n))
variables: k = number of studies; n = common per-study sample size; sigma = common SD
notes: Idealised (equal n and sigma); shows SE_M -> 0 as total sample size grows, regardless of how it is spread across studies.

name: Random-effects weight and summary SE for k equal one-group studies
variables: tau^2 = between-studies variance; k, n, sigma as above
notes: Printed as SE_M in the main text (eq. 13.2) but SE_M* in Box 13.1: the asterisk version is correct. Second term -> 0 only as k -> infinity, giving a floor of about sqrt(tau^2/k).

name: Pooled within-groups standard deviation
variables: S1, S2 = group SDs; n1, n2 = group sizes; group 1 = treated, group 2 = control
notes: Supplied from the full book only to reproduce Figs 13.1-13.2; not printed in the sample.

name: Cohen's d (standardized mean difference) and its variance
expression: d = (Xbar1 - Xbar2) / S_within ; V_d = (n1 + n2)/(n1*n2) + d^2 / (2*(n1 + n2))
variables: Xbar1, Xbar2 = group means (1 = treated, 2 = control); S_within = pooled SD; n1, n2 = group sizes
notes: Engine: smd(..., correct=False, vtype='LS2'). Not printed in the sample.

name: Hedges' small-sample correction factor J (approximation)
variables: J = correction factor; df = degrees of freedom for the within-groups SD
notes: Engine: hedges_j(df, method='approx'); the engine default is the exact gamma-function form, which differs slightly.

name: Hedges' g, its variance and standard error
expression: g = J*d ; V_g = J^2 * V_d ; SE_g = sqrt(V_g)
variables: g = bias-corrected SMD; J = correction factor; d = Cohen's d; V_d = variance of d
locator: Ch4, pp. 25-29 [NOT IN SAMPLE]; Figs 13.1-13.2, p. 78
notes: Engine: smd(..., j_method='approx', vtype='LS2') reproduces the book; default vtype 'LS' (1/n1 + 1/n2 + g^2/(2(n1+n2))) differs slightly. Ch13 recomputed g: 0.0945, 0.2774, 0.3665, 0.6644, 0.4618, 0.1852 (Carroll printed 0.10 by double rounding).

name: SE of a log ratio back-calculated from a two-sided p-value
variables: p_i = two-sided p-value; RR_i = risk ratio; Phi^-1 = standard normal quantile function
notes: Not a printed formula: it is the standard back-calculation for ratio measures (Cochrane Handbook v6, 6.3.2), used in the extraction to reproduce Fig 43.1. RR 0.80 with p = 0.265 gives SE about 0.2002, and five such trials pooled under fixed effect give p about 0.0127, printed as 0.013. Engine: se_from_p(0.80, 0.265, log_scale=True). Only valid when the p-value is exact, not given as 'p < 0.05'.

name: SE of a log ratio from its 95% confidence limits
variables: UL, LL = upper and lower 95% limits on the ratio scale
notes: Not a printed formula: it is the standard back-calculation for ratio measures (Cochrane Handbook v6, 6.3.2), used in the extraction for the new trial RR 0.91 (0.82 to 1.0), giving SE about 0.0506. Engine: se_from_ci(LL, UL, log_scale=True). Do not apply it to the misprinted meta-analysis CI '0.84 to 0.77' (p. 383).
